interval_method: conformal: 10th/90th percentiles of out-of-fold residuals from a 5-fold year-grouped split of the training years, added to the point prediction
target: onset anomaly: observed onset minus the district's fold climatology (training years, own year excluded)
shrinkage: the model's correction is multiplied by a factor in [0, 1] chosen on the same inner out-of-fold predictions (0 = the forecast is the district climatology)
contribution_method: LightGBM tree SHAP via pred_contrib=True on the anomaly model — days of onset shift away from the district climatology

imerg.name: NASA/JAXA GPM IMERG V07 daily, via NASA POWER Zarr (AWS Open Data)

power.name: NASA POWER v10 daily (MERRA-2), via NASA POWER Zarr (AWS Open Data)

nino34.name: Niño 3.4 from NASA MERRA-2 monthly skin temperature

dmi.name: Dipole Mode Index from NASA MERRA-2 monthly skin temperature

backtest: leave-one-year-out, all districts of a year held out together
label_note: Labels are the v2 onset rule — 5-day rainfall ≥ local Jun–Sep mean (2001–2025), no break ≥ 10 days under 5 mm — applied to NASA/JAXA GPM IMERG V07 (via NASA POWER) daily rainfall over DOY 121–270. Labels and the rainfall feature come from the same product, so this is a same-source nowcast check; no comparison against a third rainfall dataset has been run.

sources.labels: NASA/JAXA GPM IMERG V07 (via NASA POWER)
sources.rainfall_feature: NASA/JAXA GPM IMERG V07 (via NASA POWER)
sources.weather_features: NASA POWER daily point series (T2M, T2M_MAX, RH2M, GWETROOT)
sources.indices: Niño 3.4 (5°S–5°N, 170°W–120°W), 3-month running mean of anomalies vs 1991–2020; Dipole Mode Index (Saji et al. 1999): 50–70°E,10°S–10°N minus 90–110°E,10°S–0°, anomalies vs 1991–2020 — both from NASA MERRA-2 monthly skin temperature (TS) over ocean, via NASA POWER v10 Zarr on AWS
sources.satellite_ui: NASA GPM IMERG V07 daily (0.1°, via NASA POWER)
sources.power_rainfall_excluded: POWER PRECTOTCORR is not used for labels or the rainfall feature in the IMERG arm: at Tangail its annual total averages 937 mm in 1981–1996, 1714 mm in 1997–2015 and 2814 mm in 2016–2025, so a 45-year anomaly climatology would be measuring the product, not the monsoon. The POWER arm is therefore reported for 2001–2025 only.
sources.power_weather_note: Temperature, humidity and root-zone moisture also come from a reanalysis-merged product; they are used as anomalies against each fold's own climatology, which limits but does not remove the same inhomogeneity risk.
sources.imerg_grid: GPM IMERG is a 0.1° daily grid aggregated by NASA POWER to the UTC day: a point's value is the cell containing it, not a station reading.
sources.nasa_only: Every input is NASA or NASA-partner (JAXA, via GPM) data; no NOAA, Met Office or UCSB product is read.

out_of_sample.note: One season only, and only where the v2 rule could already confirm the onset; it is not evidence of skill on its own.

farm_district_note: A demo farm's baseline and prior-season onset come from the district it sits in; its own 1 Mar – 20 Apr rainfall comes from its own IMERG cell.
onset_rule: Onset definition v2 (local-relative 5-day accumulation, adapted from Moron & Robertson 2014)
issue_before_onset: The outlook is issued on 25 April. The v2 window opens at DOY 121 (1 May in 2026), so in some districts the real onset falls only days after the issue date: the model predicts an event that can arrive almost immediately, not one a season away.
